title: ClearScaler GTM Film
headline: Your market, worked for you.
subtitle: A silent product film for ClearScaler's GTM platform, in their dark style. The viewer's market is drawn as one live isometric map, the way Karl's reference draws a store floor, with ClearScaler's own loop on its ground. ClearScaler researches the market, scores it, writes to the accounts that fit one person at a time, and the replies come back as a meeting in the calendar. Then the loop lifts off as the 8 of the real 8% and turns into the logo.

direction.Purpose: Show what the GTM platform is and does for the viewer, muted, on the site and LinkedIn.
direction.Audience: Founders and commercial leads of B2B companies whose sales depend on the founder.
direction.Format: 16:9, 1920×1080, 30 fps, 40.0 s. Silent by brief: no voice, music or effects. Captions are the narration.
direction.Core message: ClearScaler finds the buyers who fit, writes to each one, and books the meetings into your calendar. You approve, and take the calls.
direction.Thesis: ClearScaler's GTM Engine works your whole market for you, shown on one dark map of that market.
direction.Art direction: From Karl's reference: one dark isometric world that models the domain (the viewer's market as account blocks), actors on paths, a status chip that flips, captions built word by word (grey to white), one accent colour for the product's work. ClearScaler's own motif, the hairline ∞ loop, lies on the ground from the first frame.
direction.Brand: ClearScaler's dark site: night #07080C, ink #EDEFF3, orange #FC7F48 for what ClearScaler does, green #4BC680 for replies and meetings (the app's own). Outfit, Manrope, Geist Mono. The logo stays monochrome; the orange comet over it is the site's decoration.
direction.Motion: Precise premium: the site's emphasis ease for arrivals, opacity on linear 5-frame ramps, no overshoot. The camera only breathes; the world turns 8° over the film; the one pull-back is 18% on a cosine.
direction.Transitions: Out of an object (cards unfold from their block and fold back into it); layout transformation (the rubric bars become one score bar, the score card becomes the draft); object becomes the next thing (the draft folds into the orange dot, '10:00' drops into Thursday, the ground loop lifts off as the 8, the 8 turns into the logo).
direction.Product data: The site's own demo workspace (fictional companies, labelled 'Demo workspace' on every panel, as on the site). The only real figure is the 8% reply rate, shown with its measure, window, client type, source and 'Real · anonymised'.

beats.caption: Your offer isn't the problem. Your distribution is.
beats.idea: The site's own About line. An orange comet draws ClearScaler's ∞ loop on the ground around the viewer's company while the market rises out of the dark. On 'distribution' the light contracts to a small ring: a few grey emails by hand reach the nearest accounts and stop at its edge. The rest of the market stays dark.

notes: Direction: taken from Karl's attached reference (a dark isometric world that models the domain, a status chip, captions built word by word, one accent for the product's work, a scale-out, stat, logo). Its store, palette, copy and layouts are not copied; the world here is the viewer's market, in ClearScaler's palette and type.
Karl's standing 'bright by default' is overridden by the brief, which names ClearScaler's dark style (thesis).
Every caption is ClearScaler's own copy (About, GTM Engine page, home, the logistics page's 'Run for you'): the film's words are theirs.

Product views are the site's demo workspace with fictional companies; every panel carries 'Demo workspace' as on the site. In the demo, Sofia (whose email we follow) has not replied; the reply and the meeting are Marta's, and the film shows them as two leads in one pipeline.
The only real number is the 8% reply rate (replies over 300 contacts, 12 Aug to 12 Sep 2026, campaign report, an anonymised B2B services company), as the site publishes it.

The site's hedges are kept inside the film: 'in the early months' (approval), 'Edited by our team', 'Suggested reply · edit anything before sending', 'On hold · nothing is sent'. No meeting count is implied.

The skill's busy check counts every block of the map as a separate thing (median 16); Karl's own reference reads BUSY on the same check (median 7). Clarity was judged by eye and by the reviewers instead: one focal panel at a time, the chip steps back while a card carries the beat.

The motion probe (element boxes per frame) logged duplicated, out-of-order frames under load in this sandbox; its LURCH lines were traced to those (frames 381 = 383, 384 = 385, 388 = 390). The camera measured within limits (22 px/s, 3.1 %/s). The pixel checks on the encode found no shake.

open: The 8%: the site publishes it as Real, but ClearScaler's own claims list in the site code marks it 'confirm'. Get their nod before this film is published; without it, the stat beat can be cut and the loop turned straight into the logo.

Round-2 cold eyes still finds the first 2 s too quiet for a LinkedIn scroll and wanted proof, a face or the reply up front. Kept as the site's own opening line over the market (Karl's reference opens the same way); an alternative cut could open on Marta's 'Good timing. Thursday works.' and the meeting landing, then rewind into the market.

Round-2 cold eyes asked for a 0–100 score and plainer company names; both are the site's own (scored out of 135; the demo workspace's fictional companies), so they stay unless ClearScaler wants the film to differ from the site.
The reference video's niche look was translated to ClearScaler's palette; if Karl wants the reference's yellow/blue accent logic instead of ClearScaler's orange/green, that's a token change.
A 9:16 cut for LinkedIn mobile: the stage keeps the subject inside the middle 60%, but cards would need re-layout.
Sound: silent by brief. If a version with a bed is wanted later, the cue points are the scan (4.8 s), the click (17.3 s), the meeting (26.75 s), the lift-off (31.2 s) and the logo (35.4 s).

appendix.Continuity: The viewer's block and the loop's crossing persist from 0 s to 31 s. Every card unfolds out of the block it belongs to and folds back into it (Fernhollow, Quillmoor, your block). The draft becomes the dot; the replies come back on the routes the emails took; '10:00' becomes the meeting; the loop becomes the 8; the 8 becomes the logo.
appendix.Reviews: Round 1: six independent reviews (story, truth, legibility, brand, motion on the draft, cold eyes). Round 2: a fresh cold-eyes viewer and a resolution check of the round-1 findings.
